label: Common octopus (Octopus vulgaris)

physical_parsing.volume_method: Core modelled as a mantle ellipsoid (semi-axes 0.035 x 0.035 x 0.06 m, about 3.1e-4 m3) plus head (~1e-4 m3); eight tapered arm cones (root r 0.012 m, length 0.35 m, about 5e-5 m3 each, about 4e-4 m3 total). Total about 7e-4 m3, against a sprawled bounding box of about 0.07 m3, so the solid fraction is about 1 percent.
physical_parsing.shape_class: sprawled radial (star-like) soft body: a compact mantle with eight radiating arms in a low disc

core.description: Mantle (muscular, mostly visceral mass with the gills and the jet cavity) plus the head with the eyes, and the buccal mass at the centre of the arm crown.
core.cross_section: mantle: elliptical, about 7 cm wide and 12 cm long; head: roughly circular, about 4 cm diameter

physical_parsing.size_source: Typical adult O. vulgaris: mantle length about 10 cm (larger individuals to about 20-25 cm), total arm span roughly 0.6-1.0 m (Norman 2000; Wikipedia 'Common octopus', recalled and not re-checked this session). Dimensions above are a mid-size adult and approximate.

parts.name: Arm L1 (animal's left, arm 1 from dorsal)

penetration.overlap_region: oral crown / ventral head wall at arm base; arm base is embedded in the buccal-crown ring

parts.notes: Muscular hydrostat, no rigid joints: bending is produced by transverse, longitudinal and helical muscle layers, so the joint 'pos' values are bend zones, not pivots. Two rows of suckers on the oral surface (distal to the base) give grip. Arm length is approximate (about 1.5-2x mantle length in adult O. vulgaris); range 0-180 deg per zone, distal zone allows coiling (0-360).

parts.name: Camera eye (animal's left)

penetration.overlap_region: lateral wall of the cranium / orbital cartilage

parts.notes: Image-forming camera eye, about 1 cm diameter in adults; lidless, with a pupil. Octopus eyes are largely fixed in the orbit.

parts.name: Funnel (hyponome, siphon)

penetration.overlap_region: ventral mantle wall at the head-mantle junction

parts.notes: Jet propulsion: water is drawn into the mantle cavity and expelled through the funnel. Steerable by muscle, so it orients the jet. Not a limb, so no good library match.

parts.name: Chitinous beak (upper and lower mandibles)

penetration.overlap_region: buccal mass at the centre of the arm crown, ventral

parts.notes: Parrot-like beak, hidden in the centre of the arm crown on the ventral side. Opening range is approximate. Works with a radula (not modelled).

parts.name: Interbrachial web

penetration.overlap_region: bases of all eight arms and the ventral margin of the mantle

parts.notes: Thin muscular membrane between arm bases. Used for swimming, for sheltering, and for the 'web-up' posture. Hint is by form only.

constraints.symmetry: bilateral (L/R mirror) for arms and eyes; radial-bilateral arm crown with eight arms; centre for funnel, beak, web
constraints.gait: Crawling on arms (alternating and reaching gait), with jet propulsion via the funnel for fast escape, and web-assisted swimming. Arms are the primary propulsion; the mantle is not a rigid skeletal frame.
other: No rigid skeleton: all arm bends are muscular hydrostat zones, not joints (see arm joint notes).
category_summary counts individual structures, so mirrored partners are counted (8 arms, 2 eyes).
Chromatophores and dermal papillae give colour and texture change for camouflage. They sit in the skin and are not modelled as separate parts.
Skin and ink sac are not modelled (ink is an internal defensive organ).

library_gaps.feature: Suckers (two rows per arm, with chemosensory tips)
library_gaps.why: No library part for suction cups or a sensory-tipped manipulator; hand_tentacle is the closest match for the arm but not for the sucker rows.

library_gaps.feature: Hydrostatic arm (muscular hydrostat, no rigid joints)
library_gaps.why: The library has only rigid-joint hand/foot parts; no soft-bodied, multi-zone bending arm with coil behaviour.
No library tube or nozzle part.
Colour and texture camouflage in the skin is not a geometric part; no library entry for patterned or textured skin.
Beak is covered by mouth_beak, but the internal radula has no library analogue.
No library part for a large ellipsoidal soft body; the core would need a custom mesh.
